Roche I, page 41, tune #92 ~ “Roland’s Return!” ~ Corrections

B-parts, next to the last bar, a mistake of one note raised an octave in the ABCs ~

K: Dmin ~ | G2 A BAG | AFD D2 |]

K: Emin ~ | A2 B cBA | BGE E2 |]

Admitting I’m in a mood that is decidedly minor, the tune and transcriptions here still ring as minor to my ears. The transcript I’ve given resolves for me on d, and if I push it to F it feels incomplete, unresolved. It does tend to float between modes, this I realize. The Roche settings finish final bars of both parts on D, and for me the F (or G in the transposition) doesn’t give the melody a satisfactory resolution… I did consider this when I kept finding others had been listing this tune as F Major.

It has been a pretty crazy week as I experiment with tendonitis and trying to get past my avoidance of considering the other option, the opinion of a doctor… Yes, I’m stubborn. Probably more that than shy. Are you surprised? Hey, at least twice in my life a doctor came close to killing me, once with an overdose, so maybe I have reasons for being reticent… So, maybe it is ‘shy’ rather than ‘stubborn’? It may have a lot to do with why I don’t like chemical solutions… Drugs should be a last resort, don’t you think? ;-)

↳ Posted by ceolachan on August 3rd, 2008.
